To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) there is a positive and significant relationship between HRM and firm performance in Philippine banks; and 2) there are significant differences in the relationship between HRM variables and financial performance variables.

the relationship between HRM and firm performance is significant for the Philippine banking industry, and is positive for the following HRM activities and firm financial performance indicators: (1) recruiting from top-notch schools and administering employment tests, and Assets; (2) administering employment tests, offering opportunities for professional development, and assisting in career planning, with Capital; and (3) offering opportunities for professional advancement, and assisting in the career planning process, with Deposits.
there are significant positive relationships between bank assets and bank capital and recruitment practices, but not between bank deposits and Return on Equity and recruitment practices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how human resources are managed in a bank and how this management affects bank profitability.
the impact of HRM practices on firm performance.
the relationship between HRM activities and financial performance.

the results of this study are not conclusive enough to prove or disprove the existence of any relationship between HRM activities and firm performance.
the study found a significant positive relationship between the HRM practices of recruitment, compensation, and performance management and the financial performance of Philippine banks.
there is a relationship between the HRM practices of the Philippine banks and their financial performance, but that this is not a strong relationship.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the study has found some evidence that supports the positive relationship between HR practices and financial performance.

there are significant positive relationships between HRM practices such as recruiting from topnotch institutions, administering employment tests and assisting employees in career planning and firm performance.

the results of this research provide modest evidence for a positive relationship between human resource management practices and financial performance of the Philippine banking industry, and that this relationship is more pronounced in recruitment practices than in other areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship between high performance work practices (HPWP) and firm performance is contingent upon the nature of the business.

there is a positive relationship between human resource management (HR) practices and financial performance, but that the relationship is weak, and that the HR practices are not the only factors that determine financial performance.

HRM practices and systems are important in explaining bank performance, and that these practices and systems are not just a cost center, but a potential source of competitive advantage and sustained profitability.
